column2: I gave up my post as a court singer to come here.
For the sake of your music.
Singer at the court of Cöthen. She married Bach in 1721 and bore him 13 children.
Viola da gamba sonata
I come from the court of Cöthen.
Let me support you with the sound of the gamba.
Gamba player at the court of Cöthen. His son Carl Friedrich gave concerts in London with J.C. Bach.
Tafelmusik
I have written 4,000 pieces and I am not done yet.
If you can share me with Hamburg.
In 1722 he was first choice for Thomaskantor but declined, and so Bach was chosen. Godfather to C.P.E. Bach.
Der vollkommene Capellmeister
Handel? He and I have crossed swords.
I shall back you with my critic's pen.
In 1704 he fought a duel with Handel. The point of his sword struck a metal button on Handel's coat, and Handel's life was spared.
Violin concerto
I studied with Maestro Vivaldi in Venice.
Leave the discipline of the strings to me.
He studied with Vivaldi in Venice, who dedicated several concertos to him.
Lamentations of Jeremiah
They say my music is a little strange.
Let me hold up the orchestra from the bass.
Violone player and composer in the Dresden court orchestra. Bach, too, thought highly of his works.
Flute Concerto in E minor
Let me play you the French traverso.
French flautist at the Dresden court. Teacher of Quantz, and he taught Bach's brother too.
I am giving His Highness the Prince flute lessons — in secret.
Let me pass on the secrets of the flute.
Later flute teacher to Frederick the Great, for whom he wrote some 300 flute concertos.
Rossane in Handel's Alessandro
My voice fetches a high price in London too.
I shall sing. But not on the same night as that woman.

She joined Handel's company in London in 1726; the next year her rivalry with Cuzzoni grew so heated that their partisans caused an uproar in the house and the performance was broken off. Later the wife of Hasse.
Cleopatra in Giulio Cesare
The same stage as Faustina? I decline.
I am the prima donna. On that alone I do not yield.
She created the role of Cleopatra. When she defied him in rehearsal, Handel is said to have threatened to throw her out of the window.
Cesare in Giulio Cesare
The star is I, not the composer.
If you will give me more arias.
Handel's star castrato. He clashed with Handel repeatedly and later moved to the rival company.
Everyone says my melodies are sweeter than Handel's.
Cello and composition alike — leave them to me.
He shared the favour of London with Handel. He was also a fine cellist.
Concerti grossi, Op. 3
I am a pupil of Maestro Corelli, you know.
I shall lend you a bow trained by Corelli himself.
A pupil of Corelli. He once played before the King with Handel accompanying. He was once imprisoned for debt.
Oboe concerto
The oboe is made to sing.
The oboe chair is mine.
An oboe virtuoso active in London, called the finest of his day.
Violin Sonata 'The Devil's Trill'
I am just now writing down the piece the Devil played in my dream.
If a devil's bow will do.
First violin at the Basilica of St Anthony in Padua. He said the 'Devil's Trill' was the piece the Devil played in his dream.
Vivaldi: Griselda
If the Reverend Father permits.
I shall sing on your stage.
Vivaldi's treasured singer. Her closeness to him, a priest, was often the subject of gossip.
Aria 'Son qual nave ch'agitata'
I once competed with a trumpeter to see whose breath would last longer.
I shall sing. Not for a king, but for you.
The greatest castrato in history. The story goes that he crushed a trumpeter in a contest of breath. Later he consoled the King of Spain with his singing every night.
Opera: Arianna e Teseo
It was I who trained Farinelli.
Leave the training of voices to me.
The singing teacher who trained Farinelli. Later composer to the company that rivalled Handel's in London.
Opera: Griselda (1721)
Where my son Domenico is and what he is doing, I cannot say.
I shall whip these old bones into action.
Founder of the Neapolitan school and father of Domenico. He wrote more than 100 operas.
Traité de l'harmonie (1722)
All harmony derives from the principles of nature.
I shall prove on the stage that the theory is right.
His Traité de l'harmonie of 1722 laid the foundations of modern harmonic theory. His operatic debut came in 1733, at the age of 50. He was famously thin.
Pièces de clavecin: 'Les Barricades mystérieuses'
The harpsichord must be played as though it sang.
Let me lend you a keyboard schooled at court.
A court musician since the days of Louis XIV, known as 'Couperin le Grand'. He wrote L'Art de toucher le clavecin.
Flute sonatas
Left hand or right, the flute will sing.
A flute virtuoso who made his name at the Concert Spirituel. He is said to have held the instrument the other way round.
Gradus ad Parnassum
Climb the steps of counterpoint one at a time.
If an old man will do, I shall serve as Kapellmeister.
Court Kapellmeister in Vienna. Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven all studied his counterpoint treatise of 1725. He suffered from gout.
Der General-Bass in der Composition
The Dresden orchestra is the best in Europe.
Let me show you what a court Kapellmeister can do.
Court Kapellmeister in Dresden (1717–29). He led a splendid court orchestra.
555 keyboard sonatas
Handel and I played against each other in Rome.
If the Princess gives her leave.
In 1709 he met Handel in a keyboard contest in Rome. On the harpsichord they were judged equal; on the organ Handel won. His gambling debts are said to have been paid by the Queen he served.

A giant of the symphony and a merciless conductor. Supreme in expression and theory, but with many enemies. As in real life he is driven from the Court Opera in 1907, and his life runs out in May 1911.
Salary as director of the Court Opera (+400 every month)
Symphony No. 5: Adagietto
Symphony No. 1 'Titan': finale
Lieder eines fahrenden Gesellen
My time will come.
Tradition, I have always said, is merely slovenliness.
Emperor of the tone poem and of opera, and a sharp man of business. Earn from composers' copyrights and enlarge your orchestra.
Royalties through the composers' society (+350 every month)
Also sprach Zarathustra: opening
Tone poem: Don Juan
Waltzes from Der Rosenkavalier
With what Salome earned, I built myself a villa in Garmisch.
I am a first-class second-rate composer.
Symphony No. 5
Director of the Vienna Court Opera (1897–1907). His players dreaded his unsparing rehearsals.
Also sprach Zarathustra
He worked tirelessly to found a society protecting composers' copyrights. Known as a shrewd man of business.
Debussy
Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune
In 1905 his symphonic sketches La Mer were first performed. The cover of the score used Hokusai's 'Great Wave off Kanagawa'.
Mahler: Das Lied von der Erde
I am still learning my craft under Herr Mahler.
I shall take up the baton for your orchestra.
Mahler's favourite pupil. After his teacher's death he gave the premieres of Das Lied von der Erde and the Ninth Symphony.
Verklärte Nacht
Tonality has served its purpose.
For the sake of a new music, let us join forces.
He left tonality behind from about 1908 and later devised the twelve-note method. At a concert in 1913 fighting broke out in the audience.
Liebesfreud
This little piece? I came across a manuscript by an old composer.
The scent of Vienna, for your orchestra.
He published miniatures of his own as 'arrangements of works by 18th-century composers'; his confession in 1935 caused a great stir.
Pavane pour une infante défunte
The Prix de Rome? I shall not be entering again.
I shall write you music like a precision clock.
In 1905 his elimination in the preliminary round of the Prix de Rome became a great scandal (the 'Affaire Ravel'). The director of the Conservatoire resigned and Fauré succeeded him.
Requiem
I am busy reforming the Conservatoire.
Let me lend you the power of quiet music.
Became director of the Paris Conservatoire in 1905 and taught Ravel among others. In his last years his hearing failed.
Le Carnaval des animaux
I cannot make head or tail of what the young write nowadays.
Let an old soldier show you what he can do.
At the premiere of The Rite of Spring in 1913 he is said to have left his seat in disgust at the high bassoon of the opening (the story is unverified).
Bach: Cello Suites
I spent twelve years studying the Bach suites.
The heart of the cello, for your orchestra.
At 13 he found a score of Bach's cello suites in a second-hand shop, and studied them for more than ten years before playing them in public. In 1905 he formed a trio with Cortot and Thibaud.
Chopin: 24 Préludes
Even a wrong note will do, if it is poetry.
Let me play you poetry at the piano.
In his youth he worked as an assistant on Wagner's works at Bayreuth. In 1905 he formed a trio with Casals and Thibaud.
Lalo: Symphonie espagnole
I miss the days when I played in a café.
With a sweet tone, I shall melt the stalls.
A violinist discovered while playing in a Paris café.
Madrigal
I keep faith with what Maître Taffanel taught me.
A pupil of Taffanel, later conductor at the Paris Opéra.
Debussy: Première rhapsodie
I am waiting for a new piece from Monsieur Debussy.
The clarinet chair is mine.
Professor of clarinet at the Paris Conservatoire. Debussy's Première rhapsodie (1910) is dedicated to him.
'Vesti la giubba' from Pagliacci
Do you know the magic box they call a gramophone record?
Let us sing — like the sun of Naples!
He began recording in 1902 and became the first great star of the recording age. In 1906, on tour, he was caught in the San Francisco earthquake.
Mimì in La bohème
Have you tasted the dessert that bears my name?
The queen of Covent Garden will lend you her aid.
The dessert Peach Melba and Melba toast were created in her honour by the chef Escoffier.
